issues.description: Command names in tests don't match the Python identifiers defined in commands.py
issues.detail: The methods are named `quickmarks_reload` and `bookmarks_reload` (underscores), which qutebrowser exposes as `:quickmarks-reload` and `:bookmarks-reload`. The feature tests use those hyphenated forms, which is consistent — but worth verifying against the project's naming convention (other commands use singular `:quickmark-add`, `:bookmark-add`). The naming complects two facts: the command's identity and its plurality. Pick one form across the family.

issues.description: reload() silently swallows partial-parse failures, complecting load semantics with error semantics
issues.detail: EASY-NOT-SIMPLE. `reload()` clears marks first, then re-parses. If `_init_lineparser` or `_parse_line` raises midway, the user is left with an empty or half-populated mark set and no signal about what happened. The value (old marks) and the operation (replace from disk) are entangled. Build the new map first as a pure value, then swap atomically — only emit `changed` on success.

issues.description: Parsing loop is the same code in two places via call rather than as a named pure function
issues.detail: The `__init__` now calls `reload()`, which re-clears an already-empty OrderedDict and emits `changed` during construction — a signal nobody is connected to yet, but still a semantic shift. A small pure `_parse_file(lineparser) -> OrderedDict` would let both `__init__` and `reload` consume the same value-producing function without the clear/emit dance on first load.

issues.description: Test exercises file I/O and signal plumbing instead of the parse-as-value transformation
issues.detail: TDD-AS-DESIGN. `test_reload` writes a file, constructs a manager, rewrites the file, calls reload, and asserts on `marks.items()`. It proves the wiring works but says nothing about edge cases: malformed lines mid-reload, duplicate keys, file disappearing. A pure parse function would be trivially testable against many input values without touching disk or qtbot.

issues.description: Two near-identical command methods could be one data-driven dispatch
issues.detail: `quickmarks_reload` and `bookmarks_reload` differ only in the objreg key and the message string. Not a blocker — qutebrowser's command decorator pattern makes a shared helper awkward — but the duplication is a small signal that the manager identity ('quickmark-manager' vs 'bookmark-manager') is incidental to the operation (reload from disk and announce).

review.summary: COMPLECTED in a small way: `reload()` braids three concerns — clearing existing state, re-reading the file, and emitting a change signal — with no atomic boundary, so a parse error mid-reload leaves the user with a corrupted in-memory mark set. The simple decomposition is to parse the file into a fresh immutable OrderedDict as a value, then swap-and-emit once. The duplication between `quickmarks_reload` and `bookmarks_reload` is minor and acceptable. The test proves the plumbing works but not that the parse is correct; a pure parse function would invert that. Ship-adjacent — the atomic-swap fix is the only real concern before merge.
